text:
maya: Heads-up — bringing up rook-embed-v2 on staging with int8 per-channel quant. Quick smoke looks bad for clustering/recall@50. kmeans centroids are collapsing to a couple modes.
arjun: Can you paste the eval command + data slice?
maya: Command: ```python tools/eval_embeddings.py --model rook-embed-v2 --quant int8_perchannel --dataset wikitiny --k 50 --seed 42```
maya: Quick numbers from the run: baseline fp16 recall@50: 0.842; int8_perchannel recall@50: 0.672; centroid variance (fp16 -> int8): 0.36 -> 0.09.
lisa: Oof. Did you get any clamp / saturation warnings during export or quant step?
jorge: Also can you share the UMAP/PCA plots — need to see whether collapse is global or only a subset.
maya: No clamp warnings in the quant logs. UMAP shows a dense clump for mid-length docs (20–150 tokens). Staging artifact: https://staging.artifacts/rook-v2/int8-umap.png
ciara: Could be layernorm eps mismatch or folding differences during ONNX/torchscript export. Were the normalization eps/affine params kept identical?
arjun: We saw something similar on pelican — symmetric quant + static ranges caused centroid shrink. Try asymmetric per-channel or bias-correction after quantize.
maya: Tried post-quant bias correction: recall@50 -> 0.71. Better but still below fp16. Repro snippet: ```# repro
for s in [42,43,44]:
  python tools/eval_embeddings.py --model rook-embed-v2 --quant int8_perchannel --dataset wikitiny --k 50 --seed $s
```
lisa: What's the activation distribution at key attention layers? Heavy tails -> saturation. If 99.9th pct is large, per-channel should help but maybe scales are off.
maya: Activation stats: 99.9th pct ~ 3.2, median ~0.12. Histograms uploaded in artifacts.
jorge: I'll run a controlled matrix: fp16, int8_perchannel_sym, int8_perchannel_asym, int4-lite to compute pairwise cosine shift + recall delta. Spinning up runs now.
eva-bot: Eval job queued: EVAL-874 by jorge on cluster staging-gpu (estimating ~12m)
ciara: If average cosine shift > 0.12 that's a red flag. Also check idflip@1 for short queries (<32 tokens) — we often see worst regressions there.
maya: Noted — initial breakdown shows regress concentrated on queries <64 tokens. Suspect positional/kv noise.
arjun: If pos embeddings / rotary are sensitive to quant noise, try keeping positional layers at fp16 or use higher dynamic range for those params. Also experiment with per-tensor vs per-channel for rotary matrices.
maya: OK running targeted evals: keep pos layers fp16, per-channel quant elsewhere, and one run where rotary matrices use higher-scale. Will post results in ~20m.
lisa: Thanks — if you can dump a small sample of affected queries (5–10) we can manual inspect nearest neighbor changes.
maya: Will attach them once runs finish.
lisa: :thumbsup:
